notes.meaning: The writer looks back with gratitude on what God did in earlier times. The Lord had smiled on His own land and brought His people home from captivity and ruin. Remembering God's past mercies gives believers confidence to pray for help in their present troubles.

God dealt with the real cause of His people's trouble by forgiving their sins. In Scripture, pardon means lifting off a crushing load and covering the stain of guilt completely out of sight. When God forgives His people, He does not leave any of their wrongdoing uncovered.

Because God hid their sins, He held back His burning anger. He gathered up His wrath and stopped the judgments that were ready to destroy them. When sin is taken away, God's anger turns into peace toward His people.

Facing fresh trouble, the people cry out to the God who saves them to bring them back. The greatest need in any affliction is for God to convert our hearts and turn us away from our sins. Only when we are reconciled to God can we expect His displeasure to cease.

The writer asks God with bold honesty whether His anger will last forever. God is patient and slow to anger, so His people plead that their chastisement will not be dragged out from generation to generation. Asking this question shows their deep faith that God's mercy will soon bring their suffering to an end.

The people feel faint and helpless, like dead bodies that need God to breathe fresh life into them. Revival—meaning a new giving of spiritual life and strength—is a work that only God can perform. The main purpose of this new life is that God's people may find their deepest joy in Him rather than just in their outward comfort.

The people ask the Lord to display His faithful love and grant them full deliverance. Salvation means being rescued from both the guilt of sin and its painful effects. Because this rescue is entirely a gift of divine mercy, believers can only ask for it with open hands.

After praying, the psalmist quiets his heart to listen for God's answer. He is confident that the Lord will speak peace and wholeness to His faithful followers through His Word and Spirit. At the same time, this comfort comes with a serious warning not to slip back into the foolish ways of sin.

God's rescue is close at hand for all who treat Him with holy reverence and awe. When the Lord delivers His people, His glorious presence and pure worship dwell securely in the land. Many writers also see this fulfilled in Jesus Christ, the God of glory who came to live among human beings.

God's steadfast love and His truth meet together, while His perfect justice and His peace embrace like friends. Humanly speaking, justice demands that sin be punished, while mercy begs for pardon. In God's plan of redemption, especially at the cross of Christ, divine justice is fully satisfied and mercy is freely given at the same time.

Faithfulness springs up out of the earth among renewed people, while God's righteousness looks down with favor from heaven. Heaven and earth are brought into sweet agreement under God's blessing. This also points to Jesus, who took human nature from the earth while the Father looked down on Him with complete delight.

The Lord provides everything that is truly good for His people, both spiritual grace and daily bread. When a nation turns back to God in obedience, the curse of barrenness is removed and the earth yields plentiful harvests. Spiritual renewal naturally brings the favor of God upon daily life.

Righteousness goes ahead of God like a royal herald, preparing the road for His coming in mercy. As the Lord walks before them, His righteous ways mark out the safe path for His people to follow. Many commentators also see this as a picture of John the Baptist preparing people's hearts for the arrival of Christ.
